title: Project
text:
Lock5 Stat is a gradual migration of the original Julia examples to Python on the python branch.
The notebooks use:

Polars for data loading and transformation
SciPy and NumPy for statistical calculations
great-tables for compact exploratory tables
marimo for executable, reactive notes
Quarto for the project index and published notebook library

The source data lives in data/, and shared statistical behavior is kept in marimo/lock5.py. The website restores the course layout as UnitA (chapters 1–2), UnitB (chapters 3–4), UnitC (chapters 5–6 plus case studies and exercises), UnitD, UnitE, and temp studies.


From the repository root:
./website/export-notes.sh
quarto preview website
The export step is repeatable, discovers Python notebooks under marimo/, and publishes them into the matching UnitA–UnitE or temp directory. A notebook that fails to export is skipped and reported so the rest of the site remains usable.

Source layout

title: Lock5 Stat

Start with a question
Each note keeps the original statistical idea in view while making the data, calculation, and result inspectable. The exported pages are static snapshots; the linked source notebooks remain the place to experiment.
